o1.biggest_strength: Nails the data story: sleep-led, narrator clips as core format, evening times, and a week 1 that needs no review with weeks 2-4 batched on 16 Nov.
o1.biggest_mistake: The draft-by-draft hooks are strong but a couple lean generic ('Brain still busy at bedtime?'), and the Sunday-only week-1 close doesn't explicitly flag which drafts are safe if a reviewer adds a condition term.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighter, more distinctive hooks drawn straight from customer phrases on every draft, and an explicit per-draft review-safety note.

o2.biggest_strength: Six weeks of angles in one table, real customer phrasing in hooks, and honest low/high install projections with a fatigue caveat.
o2.biggest_mistake: Says 'no post names a condition, so none needs review,' which is riskier and less careful than o1's submit-on-16-Nov approach; also the live-stream idea adds tracking risk for an owner who wants simple measures.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Adopt o1's review submission discipline and tighten the plan table so the 24-post grid doesn't sprawl.

reason: Both are strong and data-led; o1 is slightly more careful on review timing (submitting weeks 2-4 on 16 Nov rather than assuming no review) and reads a touch cleaner to act on, while o2 has the richer post range.
